newsitem.title: USA: U.S. praises Israel for "step in right direction".
newsitem.headline: U.S. praises Israel for "step in right direction".

text.p: The United States welcomed Israel's decision on Monday to ease its freeze on Palestinian Authority funds, saying the move brought the resumption of Middle East peace talks a step closer.
"We feel a little better today than we did yesterday about the prospect for getting the peace process back on track," State Department spokesman James Rubin said.

Israel freed about 30 percent of the transfers in taxes and customs duties it has withheld from Palestinian self-rule areas since a July 30 suicide bombing in Jerusalem. It said it was responding to "partial cooperation" from the Palestinians in the investigation of the attack.
Washington has criticized the blocking of the funds as an issue unrelated to security. Rubin said of Monday's move: "We welcome this decision. We believe this is a step in the right direction."

Israel says that at a meeting on Sunday with Palestinian security experts, it received the results of Palestinian checks on explosives found in early July at a suspected bomb factory for the Islamic resistance movement Hamas on the West Bank.
But Rubin and other officials said the Palestinians needed to go further in their security cooperation with Israel.

"There's a lot more that needs to be done in order to re-establish the confidence on the part of the Israelis that the Palestinian Authority is doing all it can and should do to fight terrorism," Rubin told journalists.
"We want to see more progress, and the more progress we have in that area the greater the chance that we're going to be able to move forward on the tough political decisions," he said.
Israel has called on the Palestinians to launch a major crackdown on groups like Hamas, something that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has so far refused to do.
Without specifically backing the Israeli demand, a senior U.S. official briefing reporters implicitly rejected suggestions that Arafat could not afford politically to get any tougher with Hamas.
"Those who carry out the attacks have the Palestinian Authority as their target as much as they have the Israelis as their target," he said.
"So I would say that from that standpoint, fulfilling their responsibility is something that is important for Palestinian interests."

Rubin said progress over the last two days went some way toward meeting conditions for Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to visit the region. Officials have made clear she will go only if it helps restart peace talks.
Albright is expected to make her first trip to the Middle East in September, but Rubin and other officials said she had still made no decision on the exact timing.
High-level peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians have been stalled since March, when Israel started work on a Jewish housing project in traditionally Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians have demanded an end to the work as a condition for resuming talks on the next phase of Palestinian self-rule.
